name: Lukhmi
instructions: 1. Prepare a firm dough using maida, a little ghee, and salt, then let it rest for 30 minutes.
2. In a pan, sauté onions until translucent, then add ginger-garlic paste and minced meat.
3. Add turmeric, red chili powder, salt, and garam masala, cooking until the meat is browned and dry.
4. Stir in chopped coriander and green chilies, then let the filling cool completely.
5. Roll out the dough into thin sheets and cut them into squares.
6. Place a spoonful of filling in the center, fold to form a square pocket, and seal the edges with a little water.
7. Deep fry the pockets on low-to-medium heat until they are golden brown and crispy.
description: Lukhmi is an iconic Hyderabadi delicacy often served as a starter at weddings or during evening tea. It is essentially the local variation of a samosa, distinct due to its square shape and a crisp, multi-layered dough that holds a rich, spiced meat filling.
